blocks.heading: Is Real Estate
blocks.sourceSectionTitle: Who pays, and how the money arrives

rows: Resale of a flat or house
The owner, the person buying, or both. One side is common, two sides is also common.
A percentage of the sale price. Property-portal guides put the usual figure at about 1% to 2%. No law fixes it.
Rental
The landlord, the tenant, or both.
Usually about one month of rent. Some cities push it higher, up to about three months in Mumbai and Bengaluru, say the same guides.
New project through a developer (channel partner)
The developer, usually from its own sales budget.
A commission agreed in a channel-partner agreement. We found no reliable public rate, so ask for it in writing.
Salaried sales executive at a developer or brokerage
Your employer.
A fixed salary plus incentives per booking. Pay data is thin (see the pay section).
Property or facility management
Owners, housing societies or companies.
A recurring monthly fee or a salary. Repeat revenue is the attraction.
Resale of a flat or house
You are paid only when the sale registers. Months of work can end in no payment.
Rental
Each deal is small. A rental career needs many closings, which needs a steady flow of enquiries.
New project through a developer (channel partner)
The developer sets the terms and the payout date. One vendor blog says channel partners bring roughly 10% to 15% of sales on average, so you are a side channel, not the main one.
Salaried sales executive at a developer or brokerage
Targets, site duty on weekends, and incentives that depend on the project's sales.
Property or facility management
Tenant disputes, repair problems and slow-paying clients land on you.

Real estate marketing, content and lead generation for developers and brokers
Scalable
One skill (clear listings, ads, video walkthroughs, lead follow-up systems) sells to many developers and brokers. You set the price and can add clients, then people.
Property management and rental management firm
Scalable with a business layer
Owners pay a recurring fee to have rent, repairs and tenants handled. Repeat revenue beats one-off commission.
Your own RERA-registered brokerage
Scalable with a business layer
A team, a shared listing record and a follow-up system let income grow past your own hours.
Registered valuer (land and building)
Scalable with a business layer
A licensed skill that cannot be faked. Work comes from companies and lenders who need a signed valuation.
Land and title due diligence (with advocates)
Scalable with a business layer
Clients pay to know that a property is clean before they pay for it.
Real estate marketing, content and lead generation for developers and brokers
Retainer clients and a small agency. Risk: developers cut marketing when sales slow, and payments can be late. Ads for registered projects must carry the registration number.
Property management and rental management firm
Written processes, a repair vendor list, software and hired staff. Risk: tenant disputes, repair liability and thin margins at the start.
Your own RERA-registered brokerage
Registration for the firm, GST, a CRM sheet or tool, trained agents. You carry the compliance for every deal the team does.
Channel partner for developers (new projects)
Agreements with developers, a verified client-lead process and tracking of payouts. Risk: payout delays and the developer changing terms.
Registered valuer (land and building)
A valuation firm needs several registered valuers. The route is long: degree, experience, a course and an exam (see below).
Land and title due diligence (with advocates)
The legal opinion belongs to a licensed advocate. A non-lawyer can build a document-check service that works with advocates.

blocks.heading: Compare the Practical Paths
blocks.sourceSectionTitle: The sales skills this career runs on

rows: Positioning
Pick one small area and one type of client. For example: rentals for single working people near one office cluster, or resale 2-bedroom flats in two housing societies you know well.
Write one sentence: who you help, where, and with what. Say it aloud until it takes five seconds.
A simple offer
What does the person get? Verified listings, an honest list of all costs (price, stamp duty and registration, GST where it applies, maintenance, your fee) and a written summary after each visit.
Make a one-page cost sheet template. Fill it for every property you show.
Proof
Documents checked, your RERA number on every card and advert, a short list of closed deals shared with permission, and honest reviews from past clients.
Keep a folder per property with the papers you saw. Pick one platform for your proof, such as a WhatsApp catalogue or short walkthrough videos, and post only what you have verified.
Follow-up
Most people need several conversations before a decision. The agent who writes a short recap after every visit and asks "what stops you?" stays in the race.
Every lead gets a next-step date in a sheet. No lead is left without one.
The fee conversation
Say your fee once, early and in writing, before the first visit. If someone asks you to cut it, ask what they will give in return, such as an exclusive arrangement or fewer rounds of visits.
Practise one line: "My fee is X, plus GST, and it is in our agreement before we visit." Say it without apologising.
Referrals
Real estate runs on trust in a small area. A happy client who moved in is the best moment to ask for one introduction.
After every handover or move-in, ask for one name. Keep a count of how many names you get.
Brokerage on a sale or rental (convention)
About 1% to 2% of price on a sale. About one month of rent on a rental, up to about three months in some cities.
Property-portal guides as summarised in search results (including Housing.com). Not an official source, and no statute fixes the rate.
Facilities manager, early career
Average base about Rs 3.7 lakh a year; the middle half sits between about Rs 2.1 and Rs 4.1 lakh.
Payscale India, 6 salary profiles, updated 25 July 2025. A small sample.
Commission income of agents, valuers, property managers, channel partners
No reliable public figure found.
We print none. Ask three people in your city what they earned in their first year and how many months had no income.
Housing sales, top seven cities, July to September 2026
Property trackers publish quarterly housing sales for the top cities, and in recent quarters they have not always agreed on the direction.
Sales move in cycles, and your income moves with them.
Size of the sector
Government and industry statements from 2019 to 2021 projected the sector crossing 1 trillion dollars by 2030. These are projections.
A big sector does not mean steady pay for each person in it. Read it as a long-run demand signal only.

Listing text, photo tidying, floor plans
Checking the facts. A measured carpet area and a site visit beat a generated line.
Use AI for first drafts, then correct every number against the papers.
First replies to enquiries and visit scheduling
Reading what the person really needs, and tone.
A reply template set plus a sheet. Add the personal line yourself.
Valuation estimates
A registered valuer signs and is responsible. Local knowledge decides the final number.
Data tools and clear report writing.
Reading sale deeds and approvals
A licensed advocate gives the legal opinion. You must still spot what looks wrong and ask.
A document checklist, and a habit of verifying what AI says.
Negotiation, trust, closing
All of it.
The sales skills above. Practise real conversations.
Is a degree or licence legally required?

For an agent, the rules we read ask for registration, documents and, in Maharashtra, training and an exam, not a particular degree. Check your state portal. For a registered valuer the qualification rules are strict (below). For an advocate, a law degree is compulsory.
Learn free first
Your state RERA portal, the Act and rules, regulator circulars and good YouTube channels cost nothing. Read the circulars yourself, because rules change.
The 10% simple rule

As a planning rule, not a law: if your whole education and learning budget is Rs 10 lakh, start from about Rs 1 lakh for any course or degree. Above about Rs 2 lakh you need course-specific proof, such as verified placement lists with a denominator and employers you can name.
Avoid education debt
No real estate MBA or diploma is a legal requirement for agents. Do not borrow for one. A loan taken for a course that no regulator asks for is the costly mistake.
What paid training should give you

Supervised practice, a real project, a recognised credential or access to people who hire. Not a certificate alone. Maharashtra's training is reported to be fee-capped, so compare any extra course against it.
You need a fixed monthly income starting this month
Commission arrives in lumps, and some months bring nothing. Take a salaried or facility role first and test commission on the side if your employer allows it.
You are attracted by stories of one big deal
A single large fee is the exception. Judge the route by the typical month, not the best one.
You dislike asking people to decide, or following up
Sales is about half the job. Without follow-up, most leads go quiet.
You are comfortable with "adjusting" papers or taking part cash
This career depends on trust. One cash arrangement or one forged paper can end it, and it can bring penalties and legal trouble.
You plan to borrow for a course or an office before you have a client
Registration and a phone are enough to start. Spending first is the common mistake.
You want only desk work with no talking to strangers
Valuation, document work and facility management suit this better than agent or sales work.
Class 12 student or fresher

Do not drop a degree for this. Work part time at a broker or a developer's site office during holidays, learn the state RERA rules, and build the ten-property sheet. Choose your degree for the route: civil or architecture for valuation and project work, commerce or BBA for sales and finance.
Graduate in any subject
Try a salaried sales executive role at a developer for the learning and the incentive data. Keep a record of every lead, visit and closing, because that record is your proof.
Civil, architecture or planning graduate
Valuation, project management and quantity or contract roles use your degree. Read the civil engineering guide for the lanes and pay, then add one sales skill.
Working professional wanting side income
Check your employer's rules and RERA's rules before taking any commission. Start with one area you already know, and one clear offer. Do not quit until several months of income are proven.
Family has a property or construction business
You hold an advantage in trust and land. Add systems the family business may lack: a lead sheet, written agreements, a simple cost sheet. Learn what the business pays attention to when it sells.

blocks.heading: Commission Income, with the Lumps Shown

items.text: Tax on your own earnings comes after that.

supporting: If the usual 1% is paid by one side on an Rs 80 lakh flat, the fee is Rs 80,000. GST at 18% is added to your invoice and goes to the government. It is not your income. Tax on your own earnings comes after that.

Say two months of calls, visits and follow-up end in zero closings, and the third month brings one Rs 80,000 fee. Spread over three months that is about Rs 26,700 a month. The work was steady. The pay was not.

blocks.heading: Fraud, Fake Listings and Cash Deals

figures.label: Typical Salary Range
figures.source: Cash and black money. Income tax law limits cash: an advance of Rs 20,000 or more for a property transfer and a receipt of Rs 2 lakh or more both fall under cash restrictions, with a penalty equal to the amount. These limits are described under the Income-tax Act, 1961, and the new Income-tax Act, 2025 has applied since 1 April 2026 with renumbered sections, so confirm the current section with a tax professional.
